title: I drove the old coast road at midnight. The GPS kept telling me I had already arrived.
story:
The coast road has no lights and no cell towers, so I trusted the GPS. It said forty minutes to my cousin's house.

At 12:10 it said, "You have arrived."

I stopped. The road was empty. Fog on both sides, black water below, nothing else. I tapped reroute, and the map said thirty-nine minutes. Fine. I kept driving.

At 12:25 it said it again. "You have arrived."

This time there was a mailbox on the shoulder, painted white, with no name on it. I had passed that same mailbox ten minutes ago, I was sure of it. I tried to turn the radio on and got only a slow, steady hiss.

At 12:40, the GPS voice changed. It lowered, almost gentle. "You have arrived. Please check the back seat."

I laughed, because it was ridiculous, and then I looked in the mirror.

The back seat was empty. But the seatbelt was buckled, tight, across a shape pressing the fabric out. Like someone small, sitting upright, quiet.

The little blue dot on my screen stopped moving.

Behind me, a seatbelt clicked open.

"We're here," said something warm, and very close.
premise: GPS announces arrival at a place on the empty road; the destination is behind the car
